@Tom Diem Do you think the Probabilistic Theory framework would be adapted to handle Pauli groups? Or is this something which should likely go in ./QuantumMechanics for now?

Yeah, QuantumMechanics makes sense to me. I care about complex matrix algebras more generally and I think the Pauli group and its algebra are the right starting point for the qubit. In their representation in M₂(ℂ), I, X, Y, and Z form a complex basis of M₂(ℂ) and a real basis of its Hermitian part.

I like to keep proofs abstract. For example, conjugation by Pauli exponentials gives the double-cover homomorphism from SU(2) to SO(3) and Rodrigues’ formula should follow from the algebraic relations rather than a 2 × 2 matrix calculation.

@Tom Diem Following up on this, once the abstract Pauli algebra is in place, is there interest in the stabilizer/tableau representation (the phase-free symplectic picture of the Pauli group) as the foundation for n qubit Clifford results? My end goal is entropy invariants under Clifford n-qubit operations, which fits naturally on top of that.
I do think it might be possible to build a tableau simulator formalism while the algebra is being developed.
Once we have the foundation for this, error correction codes could be added en masse

No objections from me to the tableau formalism. The entropy invariants sound interesting too. I’d like to study entropy for arbitrary states, including in infinite dimensions, but I’ve been working on other things. I think relative entropy and its monotonicity under channels would be a good place to start.

My focus is on C*-algebras, states and channels, and I may use the pure Pauli group and algebra results where they’re relevant. Error correction isn’t my focus.
